mass_properties.comment: - “Weight” values are kept in the report's stated lb units; do not silently treat them as mass in a physics equation. - Research useful load is 2927 lb for the 13000 lb gross-weight research configuration in this extraction. - The 3924 lb comparison is derived from design gross minus basic empty weight; it is not interchangeable with research useful load. - The four listed research useful-load categories sum to 2927 lb, but their original definitions still require direct table-level checking. - Source trail: S2, NASA TM-X-62407, pp. 5 and 11–12; PDF URL recorded in sources.xml.

inertia_calculation_readiness.available_component_group_weights: Group weights are listed above, but they are not component centre-of-mass coordinates or component own-axis inertia tensors.
inertia_calculation_readiness.missing_inputs: Pylon spindle station and water-line coordinates; baseline CG water line; pylon/nacelle/rotor assembly centre of mass relative to the conversion axis; moving assembly inertia tensor; fixed-airframe inertia tensor; mass distribution and configuration details consistent with the selected endpoint inertias.
inertia_calculation_readiness.caution: Do not convert weights into component masses/inertias or infer missing locations without source-supported definitions and units.

mass_moments_of_inertia.comment: - Ixx, Iyy, and Izz are rotational mass moments of inertia about the stated body axes. - Unit slug*ft^2 measures resistance to angular acceleration about each axis; these are not weights. - The supplied dataset reports airplane and helicopter/hover endpoints only. - Intermediate nacelle-angle values and a source-supported transformation method were not provided. - Source trail: S2, NASA TM-X-62407, p. 12, sec. 3.1.3. - PDF: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19750016648/downloads/19750016648.pdf
